question: I want a site that's in one of my teams to show up under my personal sites instead
reference_answer: In the site's settings, go to Danger zone, choose My personal sites under Transfer site and click Move site. It moves immediately, and your personal account needs an active subscription that supports the extra site.
key_facts: Danger zone > Transfer site > My personal sites > Move site
Personal account needs an active subscription supporting the site
answer: To transfer a site from a team to your personal sites, go to the site settings for that site, click Danger zone in the left sidebar, select My personal sites under Transfer site, and click Move site [1].

4. Click **Move site**

evidence.title: Transfer ownership of a site
evidence.text:
If a site is currently part of a team but you want it to appear under **My personal sites**, you can transfer the ownership to yourself.

1. Go to site settings for the site you want to move
2. Click **Danger zone** in the left sidebar
3. Under **Transfer site**, select **My personal sites**
4. Click **Move site**

The site moves immediately to your **My personal sites** section. Your personal account must have an active subscription that supports the additional site.

question: If I don't enter a card during the free trial, will I be charged when it ends?
reference_answer: No. No credit card is asked for at registration, so there's no payment method to charge and the trial never converts into a paid subscription automatically. There's nothing to cancel.
key_facts: No credit card is required
Trial never converts automatically
Nothing to cancel
answer: We don't ask for a credit card when you register, there's no payment method on file, and your trial never converts into a paid subscription automatically [1].

citations.quote: We don't ask for a credit card when you register. There's no payment method on file, so we can't charge you. Your trial never converts into a paid subscription automatically.

evidence.title: How the free trial works
evidence.text:
Every Plausible account starts with a free 30-day trial. During the trial you have access to all Business plan features and limits, so you can explore the full product before choosing a plan.

## No credit card, no automatic charges

We don't ask for a credit card when you register. There's no payment method on file, so we can't charge you. Your trial never converts into a paid subscription automatically.

This also means there's nothing to cancel. If you don't want to continue after the trial, you don't need to do anything.

## What happens when the trial ends

If you haven't subscribed by the end of the trial, your dashboard is locked. You can still log in to your account.

We don't keep your website analytics data indefinitely after your trial ends.

If you don't subscribe, we'll stop collecting new stats and eventually delete your dashboards and all their stats permanently. We'll email you before deletion so you have time to subscribe or export your stats.

After your trial ends, we keep recording stats for a few more days, and the email we send when the trial expires says how many. Recording stops at midnight UTC on the last of those days.

Automatic deletion removes your sites and stats, but your login stays until you delete your account.

Subscribe before deletion to unlock your dashboards and keep your historical stats. Deleted stats cannot be recovered.

## Delete your account at any time

You can delete your account with a few clicks at any point, during or after the trial. Go to **Account settings**, scroll to the **Danger zone** section and click **Delete Account**. This removes all your sites and collected stats.

To start a new 30-day trial, delete your account and sign up again with the same email.

question: Our PDFs are hosted on a CDN and they don't show up in my file downloads goal. Why?
reference_answer: Automatic file download tracking only works for files hosted on the same domain as the tracked site. Files served from a CDN, another domain or an untracked subdomain are tracked as outbound link clicks instead.
key_facts: File download tracking only works for files on the same domain as the site
Files on a CDN or other domain are tracked as outbound link clicks
answer: Automatic file download tracking only works for files hosted on the same domain as the tracked site [1]. Files served from a CDN are tracked as outbound link clicks instead [1].

citations.quote: Automatic file download tracking only works for files hosted on the same domain as the tracked site. Files served from a CDN, another domain, or an untracked subdomain will be tracked as outbound link clicks instead.

evidence.title: File downloads tracking
evidence.text:
Note:
Automatic file download tracking only works for files hosted on the same domain as the tracked site. Files served from a CDN, another domain, or an untracked subdomain will be tracked as outbound link clicks instead.

Our **File downloads** tracking captures a file download event each time a link is clicked with a document, presentation, text file, compressed file, video, audio or other common file type. Both internal and external files downloads are tracked. These file extensions are tracked by default:

`.pdf`, `.xlsx`, `.docx`, `.txt`, `.rtf`, `.csv`, `.exe`, `.key`, `.pps`, `.ppt`, `.pptx`, `.7z`, `.pkg`, `.rar`, `.gz`, `.zip`, `.avi`, `.mov`, `.mp4`, `.mpeg`, `.wmv`, `.midi`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.wma`, `.dmg`

Note that clicks on download links within `svg` elements are not tracked.

A link is detected as a file download by the file extension at the end of its path, such as `/files/report.pdf`. Some CMSs serve files from addresses without an extension, such as `/web/content/1234`, so clicks on those links aren't detected. To track them, add a CSS class name to the link and track it as a custom event.

question: Can I make a goal that only counts Sign Up events for the pro plan? And is there a limit to how many properties I can attach to a goal?
reference_answer: Yes. When creating a custom event goal you can attach property constraints, so for example a `Pro Sign Up` goal fires only when a `Sign Up` event includes `plan=pro`. You can attach up to three property constraints to a goal definition.
key_facts: Property-filtered goals only count events whose name and property values match
Example: Pro Sign Up goal matches Sign Up with plan=pro
Up to three property constraints per goal
answer: Yes, you can create a goal that only counts Sign Up events for the pro plan by attaching property constraints to the goal definition [1]. When creating a goal from a custom event in your site settings, you can optionally attach up to three property constraints to that goal [1].

citations.quote: When you create a goal from a custom event in your site settings, you can optionally attach up to three property constraints to that goal definition.

evidence.title: Custom properties for events
evidence.text:
When you create a goal from a custom event in your site settings, you can optionally attach up to three property constraints to that goal definition.

A property-filtered goal only counts an event when both the event name and the property values match. For example, you can create a `Pro Sign Up` goal that only fires when a `Sign Up` event includes `plan=pro`. A separate `Starter Sign Up` goal would match `plan=starter`.

This is distinct from simply sending properties with your events:

- **Sending a property with an event** records raw data. You can filter and analyze it in the dashboard after the fact.
- **Attaching a property to a goal** makes the property part of the goal's definition. The goal only counts when that specific property value is present. It becomes a discrete conversion metric, not a filtered view of existing data.

question: I added the 404 snippet and created the goal but the 404 goal shows no conversions. What could be wrong?
reference_answer: Check that the code is in your dedicated 404 error page template and not just the main layout, and that the goal in site settings is named exactly `404`. Test by visiting a URL that doesn't exist and watching the realtime view, and if your site is behind a CDN or cache, purge it because the 404 template may be cached without the new code.
key_facts: Code must be in the dedicated 404 template
Goal name must match `404` exactly
Purge any CDN or cache after the change
answer: Code not in the right template: Ensure your custom code is in the dedicated 404 error page template rather than just the main layout [1]. Goal name mismatch: The goal name in your site settings must match the event name `404` in your code exactly [1]. Caching: If your site uses a CDN or caching layer, purge your cache after adding the new code [1].

citations.quote: Most platforms have a dedicated 404 error page template (often called 404.html, error.html or similar). Confirm your custom code is in that specific template and not just added to the main layout.

evidence.title: 404 error pages tracking
evidence.text:
If you have set up the 404 goal but see no data, check the following.

**Code not in the right template.** Most platforms have a dedicated 404 error page template (often called `404.html`, `error.html` or similar). Confirm your custom code is in that specific template and not just added to the main layout. Visit a broken URL on your site to verify the 404 page loads correctly.

**Goal name mismatch.** The goal name in your Plausible site settings must match the event name in your code exactly. The code uses `404` as the event name by default. Check your site settings to confirm the goal is named `404`.

**Testing with a real 404 URL.** After adding the code, visit a URL on your site that does not exist (for example `/this-page-does-not-exist-test`). Open your Plausible dashboard and check the realtime view. You should see a `404` conversion appear within a few seconds. If it does not appear, open your browser's Network tab and look for a request to `plausible.io/api/event` to confirm the event is firing. For more general script troubleshooting steps, see troubleshooting your integration.

**Caching.** If your site is behind a CDN or caching layer, the 404 page template may be cached without the new code. Purge your cache after making the change.

question: I got a huge traffic spike yesterday from a country we don't even sell to. How can I tell if it's bots?
reference_answer: Filter the dashboard to isolate the spiking source, country or page and check the bounce rate and visit duration. Bot traffic almost always shows a near-100% bounce rate and zero visit duration, while meaningful time on page, scroll depth and conversions suggest real visitors. You can also check the Sources tab, entry pages and the Hostname filter.
key_facts: Bot traffic almost always has a near-100% bounce rate
Visit duration reads as zero for bounced visits
Check Sources, entry pages and Hostname to identify the source
answer: To determine if a traffic spike is from bots, apply a filter to isolate the country that spiked [1]. Bot traffic almost always shows a near-100% bounce rate, and visit duration will read as zero [1]. If the filtered view shows meaningful time on page, scroll depth, and goal conversions, the traffic is more likely to be real [1].

citations.quote: Apply a filter to isolate the traffic source, country or page that spiked. Bot traffic almost always shows a near-100% bounce rate. Visit duration will also read as zero since bounced visits count as 0 seconds in Plausible. If the filtered view shows meaningful time on page, scroll depth and goal conversions, the traffic is more likely real.

evidence.title: Bot and spam traffic filtering
evidence.text:
If you see an unexpected spike in your dashboard, run through these steps to confirm whether it is bot traffic and block it.

### 1. Check bounce rate and visit duration

Apply a filter to isolate the traffic source, country or page that spiked. Bot traffic almost always shows a near-100% bounce rate. Visit duration will also read as zero since bounced visits count as 0 seconds in Plausible. If the filtered view shows meaningful time on page, scroll depth and goal conversions, the traffic is more likely real. Note that low-quality traffic is not the same as bot traffic: real visitors can arrive from the wrong source or with expectations the page does not meet, producing low engagement without being automated. Plausible's filters target non-human visits only.

### 2. Identify the source

Look at the **Sources** tab to see where the spike is coming from. Common patterns for bot traffic:

- A single referrer domain you don't recognise
- Direct traffic spiking with no accompanying change in referral or search traffic
- A specific country sending a sudden burst with no prior history

### 3. Check the entry pages

Look at the **Pages** tab filtered to the spike period. Bots often hit a single page repeatedly or target unusual paths like `/wp-admin`, `/xmlrpc.php` or random URL strings.

Filter by **Hostname** too. If the spike was recorded on websites that aren't yours, those pageviews were sent to your dashboard from other sites.

question: I keep applying the same filters for my UK mobile visitors. Can I save that combination so my team can reuse it?
reference_answer: Yes. After setting up your filters, click the Save as segment (star icon) next to the filter pills, choose a personal segment (only you) or a site segment (visible to all team members with dashboard access), name it and save. Later you can open it from the Segment entry in the Filter menu.

answer: Yes, you can save your filter combination as a segment so that your team can reuse it [1]. After completing your segment, click the save option and choose "site segments" so it is visible to all team members with access to your dashboard [1].

evidence.title: Filter and segment your audience
evidence.text:
Click on any metric in the dashboard or use the **Filter** button to filter your audience to a desired segment. After completing your segment, click the **Save as segment** (star icon) option next to the filter pills.

Save as segment star button beside the active Entry page and Channel filters

Segments can be saved either as "personal segments" (these are visible only to you) or as "site segments" (these are visible to all the team members that have access to your dashboard).

Choose the type of segment you want to create, give it a recognizable name and click on the **Save** button.

### How to open a previously saved segment

Click the **Filter** button and open **Segment** to view your saved segments. Click on a segment to open it in your dashboard.

Saved segments listed in the Segment submenu of the Plausible Filter menu

The **Segment** entry is only visible after you save your first segment.

### How to edit or delete a previously saved segment

Open a previously saved segment and click its pill at the top of your Plausible dashboard. From this menu, you can view its filters, switch to another segment, edit, duplicate or delete the segment.

Select **Edit segment** to add, remove or change filters. Click **Save** to update the segment or **Cancel** to return to the saved version.
